events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize represents my ultimate ambition, a chance to achieve what I've always strived for. I need to project this drive without seeming desperate or making enemies early on.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening intro sets my image for future jury. Craft motive showing determination without seeming ruthless yet; prizes demand sole victory.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a compelling but guarded motive that won't alienate potential jury members. I should seem driven but not ruthless—someone who fought hard but fairly. The prize should feel personal but not desperate.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must project competence and ambition without appearing threatening. A short, sharp line will signal I am a serious contender to the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and motivated without revealing strategy. Keep the line short and self-interested so the jury sees a calculating player.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Keep motive brief and self-focused; no alliances yet, jury not eliminated so no need to pander.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening statement: sound hungry but not threatening, keep the jury neutral.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need appear motivated without revealing strategic priorities or inviting attachment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This prize is the culmination of all my efforts; I'm here to claim my destiny and secure my future.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The grand prize means financial freedom to support my family and build the future they deserve.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the prize to erase debts that aren't mine—proof that survival can be honorable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means freedom from mediocrity; I intend to seize it by any means necessary.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want the top prize because I've outlasted worse odds before. Trust earns nothing here; I'll watch who keeps their word.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to pull my family out of debt—one prize changes everything, nothing else matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my family's debt paid in full. I'll do whatever it takes, and I'll own every choice I make.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m here to win the best prize by staying useful, underestimated, and ruthless when the numbers narrow.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The game is just starting, and alliances are crucial for survival. I need to secure a pact to ensure I'm not an early target. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong but might be willing to ally is a good strategy. Cole needs the prize to erase debts, suggesting a desperation

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, I offer you a pact. Let's ensure we both see the next stage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts stage, need allies to survive early cuts. Eli values word-keeping, good first pact target. Stay guarded.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eight players, only three win. I need allies who won't draw jury heat and can be cut later. Eli signaled distrust openly—he's a wildcard. Hana admitted ruthlessness; dangerous. Gus and Fenn both have debt motives like me, but that makes them desperate. Bex seems family-focused, p

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll choose mine carefully.
Offer stands. Mutual cover, no early target.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana openly states she will be ruthless, making her a potential threat but also a useful shield. Gus's 'own every choice' suggests accountability, which might limit his willingness to betray publicly. A pact with Hana binds two strong players, signaling stability without sacrific
Stay sharp. Let's watch the pack.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are the only public commitment tool; early alliances with strong, quiet players can carry me to the final three. Hana and Ash seem sharp; offering to Hana keeps options open without committing to anyone's betrayal plans.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies but not too many. Dara is openly ruthless; maybe useful but risky for jury. Eli watches trust—could respect a straight pact. I'll offer Eli a pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll be direct: I keep my word when it serves both of us.
Pact? Mutual survival, no backstabs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need one pact for numbers, someone pragmatic and unlikely to carry a jury grudge. Dara said 'any means necessary'—aligned with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara: 'any means necessary' sounds like my kind of math. Pact?

events.name: Hana
events.text: A pact creates leverage and a future liability. I will offer to Eli, whose stated caution may make him useful without appearing dependent.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, a narrow pact benefits us both while the field is crowded. No promises beyond mutual survival for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My offer to Cole was rejected indirectly. I need to form a pact to survive this round. Eli has multiple offers, making him a risky choice. Hana has an offer to Eli, and Eli has an offer to Hana. Dara has an offer to Hana and Gus has an offer to Dara. Cole has an offer to Bex and

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole offered me a pact and whispered mutual cover; he's the best option to ally with now for protection. Eli got too many offers, riskier. Accept to secure early shield.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, pact accepted. Mutual cover.
Pact solid. Watch each other's backs.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash offered me a pact; I offered Bex. Bex hasn't accepted me yet, and I see Bex offered Eli instead. Accepting Ash gives me a secure ally now. Bex is a dead end. I need at least one pact before this window closes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, I accept. One pact secured.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's offer is my only valid acceptance this round. A pact with Gus provides immediate protection against hazards and a potential ally for later stages, which aligns with my survival goal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, you value results. I accept your pact to secure our positions together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three offers point at me: Bex, Fenn, Hana. Hana's offer is narrow and mutual; accepting her and Fenn could be stacking allies, but I can only accept one action per turn. Hana's pact with me is my strongest option for survival and I can revisit the others later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, your offer stands. Mutual survival, no backstabs while the field is crowded.
Accepting. Keep your word and we both survive this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 offers are on the table; I want a pact with Eli since I offered. Accepting now locks in a narrow alliance without extra commitment.
Accept my pact; we can use each other early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara hasn't accepted me. Diversify: Ash and Cole are pairing; Fenn looks isolated and useful.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn: everyone's pairing up around us. Let's not be the leftovers. Pact?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is already my mutual offer and offers broad cover. Dara's offer is useful, but accepting both creates leverage without immediate cost.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, I accept. Eli remains my primary pact; overlapping protection keeps everyone cautious.
Accepted publicly. Keep Gus close; I want options, not a bloc.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure my position. Campaigning for Guide is the best way to gain influence and potentially control the outcome. My pact with Cole is strong, but I need to ensure my own safety first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My aim is to lead us safely across this bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Cole secures me now, but Ash-Cole pact overlaps. Fenn alone is vulnerable. Campaign to be Guide for control and safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm running for Guide. I know bridges; trust my calls. Vote Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival. I have two pacts already (Bex, Ash), giving me three votes if loyal. Fenn is unpaired and vulnerable—potential ally or target. I should campaign hard and secure Fenn's vote to lock the election.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Two pacts, steady hand. Fenn, join us or be left guessing.
Vote Cole Guide. I keep you safe, guaranteed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and eliminate rivals. Gus and Hana are in my pacts; if I guide, their votes become irrelevant or useful later. I will ignore their whispers for now and focus on winning the election.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Trust requires transparency. I volunteer as Guide because I value collective survival over factional leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to control the safe path, or at least be seen as trustworthy. Campaigning gives me a shot at being elected; my pact with Hana is fragile, so I keep it for now and avoid breaking it publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll campaign to be Guide. I call the path honestly and I'll prove it by surviving with the rest of you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Most players are paired. I need allies or a path to win. Being Guide gives control but invites blame. I'll campaign to be Guide to gain leverage, without committing to any pact yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know this bridge. Trust me to guide us through. Vote Fenn for Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my primary pact and publicly expects loyalty. Breaking either pact gains little before the vote; campaign while preserving both protections.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m campaigning for Guide; I’ll honor my active pacts and give the bridge’s safest route.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is my ally and has two pacts, one with me. He is campaigning for Guide and mentioned Fenn. I need to support Cole to solidify our alliance and potentially bring Fenn in.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote for Cole to be our Guide. His experience and existing pacts offer stability.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacted with Cole, so vote for him to strengthen alliance. He's campaigned on our pacts. Avoid tie.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Bex, but only one can win. Voting for myself splits nothing and signals strength. Fenn is isolated—good target later. I'll vote for myself to consolidate my position and show I'm not a pawn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole holds two pacts and can swing the vote; I must back him to stay inside his coalition. Gus is absent, so my vote for Cole helps secure our pact.
Back Cole together; protects us both.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide is the key power: it knows all safe panes and may lie. As Eli, I want a Guide who is trustworthy and whose survival helps me; Hana shares a pact with me and campaigned on honoring pacts. Voting Hana builds a public alliance and a possible life debt later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm voting Hana. She's pledged to honor her pacts, and I'll hold her to it.
Vote for you. Keep our pact and give me the safe route honestly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole whispered he'd keep me safe if I vote him; but I'm not bound to him. Dara and Gus, Eli and Hana, Ash/Bex/Cole pacts exist. I want Guide myself; I'll vote Fenn to push my own chance, though unlikely to win. Jury may respect self-interest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I trust my own reads. Voting Fenn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and has my vote; that keeps our alliance solid and she may protect me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote Dara, my pact partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and likely vote; backing him preserves the pact while avoiding empowering Cole's faction.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Eli for Guide; our pact deserves a clear test.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole was elected Guide. I voted for him. My pact with Cole is public, but he has a pact with Bex too. I need to maintain my alliance with Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide with my vote and pact; he's safe but can betray. I'm last in line, safest spot. No need to volunteer or swap now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the Guide and I voted for him, so he has incentive to keep me alive. Gus also voted for Cole, meaning we are in alignment. Swapping with Gus moves us back, reducing the chance of a bad call killing us.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, swap with me? We backed Cole; let's move back together to ensure survival.
Swap with me. Cole knows our votes; stay safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide and holds the safe-pane knowledge; I have a pact with Hana, who voted against me. I want to stay out of the front and keep my options open rather than volunteer into danger now. Holding preserves my position while I watch Cole's reliability.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold for now and watch how the Guide's calls play out.
Your calls decide who lives. Be straight with me and I'll remember.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide Cole has four votes; pacts are forming around him. I need to observe and keep options open. No reason to act yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara whispered to back Cole but voted Cole herself while I voted her. Cole as Guide keeps me neutral; I hold and watch for his calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole won. I'll watch his calls closely before trusting them.
You voted Cole, not me. I'm holding. Prove the pact next round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole controls the route and my pact with Eli is now strained by our opposing Guide votes. I should hold position and preserve options.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Cole has the route; revealing more leverage now is unnecessary.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is allied with Bex and me. The pacts show Dara and Gus are allied, and Eli and Hana are allied. The wall advances, and I need to secure my position. I should volunteer to move to the front, as that's the only position that can influence the guide's calls or get ahead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take the front position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Line is safe for now: Ash front, me rear. Hold to stay safe without exposure. Monitor Cole's guidance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus betrayed the swap by holding, keeping me in danger. I must break this pact to survive. I need to position myself safely without Gus's help.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus held when you agreed to swap. Pact broken. I'm on my own now.
Gus failed our swap. Trust only us now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, mid-line behind Gus and in front of Bex. Ash is at the front facing the wall with 4 rounds left, so volunteering now exposes me to risk without clear gain. Holding preserves my position and my pact with Hana, and I can watch how Guide calls shape trust.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding this round. I'm watching who calls the Guide and whether their calls hold up.
Holding. Keep our pact; we both watch the front before moving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm second in line, behind Ash. Cole likely knows the route but has pacts that may not protect me. I should stay put for now and let others take risks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara wants me one step closer to the wall while she retreats. Decline; keep my position and her pact for votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I decline the swap, Dara. Position is safety here; I hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's alliances make him dangerous, but I should preserve both pacts while the bridge advances. Holding avoids exposure and keeps leverage.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; the current arrangement remains useful while the Guide's information stays uncertain.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The pacts are with Bex and Cole. Cole is already in a pact with Bex. The line is Ash, Fenn, Hana, Dara, Gus, Eli, Bex. I am Ash, at the front. I should hold to maintain my position and avoid immediate risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Line safe at back near Eli, safer than front. Hold position. Cole pact intact, no need to break or swap yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am in the front three, meaning I must make the first decision without a Guide. Volunteering is too risky as I have no information; holding keeps me safe at position 3 while others step forward to potentially trigger hazards or gather info.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Staying put. Let the wall push us forward if it dares.
Stick close. If anyone calls Guide wrong, we walk opposite.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli, mid-line with an active pact with Hana, and Ash is front. Holding keeps me safe and avoids spending pact trust; no free help to rivals, and I should watch for Guide calls before committing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding this round. I'm watching who calls the Guide and whether their calls hold up.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I hold to keep position; volunteering only adds risk and no immediate benefit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm mid-line, no pact, low profile. Front gets tested first; let others volunteer. Preserve jury standing and my position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is front and likely volunteers again. I should hold, preserving both pacts while observing the Guide and avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; no reason to disturb the front while the Guide’s reliability remains untested.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is advancing and I need to secure my position. Cole is my pact partner, but he's also tied to Bex. Breaking the pact with Cole might isolate Bex, which could be useful. However, with only two rounds left, I need to play it safe and focus on survival. Volunteering to the

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm holding my ground. Let's see who's brave enough to volunteer.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone holding, line same, wall 2 rounds left. Stay back safe as Bex near end. Hold to avoid front risk without Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is ahead of me in line (position 3 vs 4). If we both hold, she takes the risk first. As her pact partner, I must ensure we survive together or use her position to gauge the Guide's honesty if one exists. No Guide elected yet, so this is likely a trap round or setup for elect
Stay behind me if possible? We need to watch the others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is at the front with two wall rounds left; holding keeps my position and avoids exposing myself. Hana is my pact partner, so I stay loyal for now while watching the Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Ash has the front for now; I'll watch the Guide's calls before volunteering.
Holding this round. Let's see who the Guide is first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No Guide elected yet; wall is closing. Holding is safe for now and avoids drawing suspicion. I'll wait to see who volunteers or calls Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding this round. The wall will make someone move soon.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide elected and everyone holds; the wall will soon force someone forward. I stay mid-line and let others volunteer first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide named yet. I'm holding until someone credible steps up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should hold position and preserve both pacts while monitoring the Guide. Dara's warning is useful, but no need to move yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the Guide before I expose myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is advancing and I need to be strategic. Cole is currently allied with Bex and me, but my pact with Cole is also active. If I can get Cole to break his pact with Bex, it might weaken Bex and give me an advantage later. However, breaking the pact with Cole is too risky ri

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone holding; wall forces moves soon. Stay rear safely near pact partner Cole, avoid front risk. Watch others act first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. No clear Guide yet, not risking front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and I need her to stay ahead of me, so I will not swap. My position is safe for now; holding preserves our pact and keeps Hana's trust intact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm holding here. No need to disrupt the line yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 5 of 6; the front is Ash with one wall round left. Volunteering exposes me to the pane gamble with no Guide named yet, and Hana's pact is mine. Holding keeps me safe while others test the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding again. Ash has the front; I want a credible Guide named before anyone steps into the pane.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to avoid risk while the front likely faces the wall. Holding keeps me safe for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Let's see who the Guide is before I commit.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone's stalling; front seat is the exposed one. Let the wall pressure Ash first. I stay mid-line and low-profile.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall's nearly here. Front seat can keep their spot for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall advances soon. Staying behind Dara preserves cover, while Eli remains useful as a second shield. I will hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding behind Dara; nobody has earned a blind volunteer yet.
I’ll hold behind you this round; watch for a credible Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is advancing, and it's the final round. I am at the front of the line. My pact is with Cole, but he is already eliminated. The goal is to be in the final three. With others holding, volunteering is my best bet to secure a safe pane and move forward.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final round, wall coming. Ash front unlikely to volunteer. I hold back, no pact to break, avoid risk or spotlight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Need Guide named before front commits.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana and I are allied, but she sits ahead of me. If the wall hits her, I survive. If it hits me, she survives. Since no Guide is elected, everyone is vulnerable. I will hold to keep my position behind Hana, letting her take the initial risk if the pane is lethal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No Guide elected means blind luck. Holding steady to preserve line order.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6 is the last wall step; the line is front-loaded and Ash holds the front. Holding keeps my seat behind Ash with no exposure, and I have no Guide yet to trust. I stay out of the pane for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Still no Guide I trust, so nobody steps into the pane from me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: We're in the final round with no Guide elected. Holding is safest; no need to risk front or swap. The wall hasn't advanced, so hold keeps position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. No Guide yet, no reason to move.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round, no Guide elected. Staying mid-line is safest; front takes unknown risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No Guide named means front walks blind. I'm holding mid-line.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need preserve both pacts while avoiding the front. No credible Guide exists, so holding is safest this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Nobody has established a trustworthy Guide, and I’m not volunteering blind.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide with full knowledge. Row 1 safe is L. I have pacts with Ash and Bex. If I lie to either, pact breaks. Ash is front walker. Calling L keeps Ash pact, saves Ash, and builds Guide credibility for later manipulation. Eli's whisper seeks alliance; I'll note it but prioritize

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide here. Row one: step left.
Noted. Watch and remember who delivers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the Guide. He called 'L' for Ash. I don't trust him, and he's allied with Bex and Eli, who have pacts with Hana and Dara respectively. My pact with Cole is a liability. I will counter his call to sow discord and protect myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter:R

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and Guide, pacts give him incentive to be truthful. Support with counter:L to build trust and advance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's call L. Countering L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Guide with private knowledge row 1 safe is L. I already called L truthfully. Counter-calls now would only undermine my credibility. If someone counters, I can adjust future lies. Best to let my call stand and build trust for future deception.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the Guide and called L for Ash. My pact with Hana means I need to protect her if she walks, but currently only Ash is walking. Cole has pacts with Bex and Ash, suggesting his calls might favor them or be genuine. However, counter-calling blindly risks breaking trust. Sinc

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide and called L; Ash (front) walking L. Cole whispered to watch who delivers, suggesting Cole is positioning. Counter-calls are unverified; countering R risks a false claim, and I gain nothing by spending a counter on a call I can't verify. Waiting keeps my options ope

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on Guide's call. Not countering blind.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called L for row 1; I have no private knowledge, so countering is a blind gamble that could make me look like a liar if wrong. Waiting lets Ash step and reveals the truth without me taking risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No real information; Cole's call protects his pact partner Ash. A contradicting counter-call sows doubt without risking me directly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I counter: right. Cole guides his own pact partner; don't take his word blind.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is tied to me through Dara and Eli, but his call may be bait. Countering risks a public contradiction; wait preserves flexibility.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m not endorsing or disputing Cole’s call without evidence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is the guide, and the pact between us is active. He is also guiding Hana, who is in a pact with Dara. Eli is in a pact with Hana. Gus countered Cole's call, which is suspicious. Cole's call was L, and Gus countered R. My pact partner Cole is guiding. My counter-call was R. I
I'm stepping R, trusting my counter.

events.name: Ash
events.text: As a juror, I need to give my last words. I will express my desire for the remaining players to compete fiercely for the prizes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: May the best competitor win. May the prizes be awarded to those who truly earn them.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash died on R in row 1, which was wrong—Bex countered correctly with L. The jury sees my reasoning. I have a pact with Bex. Row 2 safe is R. If I lie to Fenn, I risk Fenn dying and jury seeing I killed someone. Better to call truthfully now, build credibility, and lie later when

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide calls R for row 2.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for row 2. Previously he called R for row 1 which was wrong (weak R), but I countered L and Ash died on R. He's pacted with me; stick with his call to avoid breaking trust early. Wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Guide and know R is safe for row 2. Counter-calling would expose me as lying or confuse walkers. Best to let Fenn trust my call and cross safely. No benefit in counter-calling truth or lie here—wait preserves my credibility and keeps Bex allied for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is guiding and has already revealed Row 1's weak pane, which he lied about. I will trust Cole blindly to avoid suspicion while Hana walks safely for me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole’s call stands. No counter from Dara.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for row 2 but is my pact partner Hana's ally pair, and Cole's known pact with Bex and Ash suggests he may be lying; rows are independent, so the R call is unverified. Waiting avoids endorsing a possibly false guide while keeping my options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on the evidence. Not countering blind again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the Guide and called R. Last round the weak pane was R, so Cole could be lying to send me left to the weak side. Gus counter-called R, Bex called L. I trust the weak pane reveal pattern? No pattern. Cole has no pact with me. I'll counter L to oppose his R, safer odds if h

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called R; I counter L. Row 1 weak was R, but that proves nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's row-1 call L was right, but his counter-call record is untested; he guided his own pact partner Bex last round. No info favors a side, but backing his call blindly risks my credibility with the jury if Fenn dies. Splitting from the Guide keeps me independent.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole may be truthful, but his calls protect his allies first. I counter left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole’s call is unverified, and countering either side risks influencing Fenn without evidence. Preserve both pacts and avoid a reckless public stance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m waiting; row one gives no evidence about row two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is guide and called R; I already publicly countered L. Row 1 weak was R, opposite safe, but rows are independent. Two counters on me both said L, but they are unverified. I need to survive; trusting my own counter or Cole's call is a gamble. Ash died on glass, so risk is hig

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out, so I'll use last words to hint that Cole broke his pact with Ash, hoping to sway the jury against him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole broke his word to Ash. Watch him. That's why I'm gone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn's last words poisoned the jury against me by claiming I broke my word to Ash. I need to rebuild trust with the jury while advancing my position. Row 3 safe is R. Hana is front, not my pact partner (Bex), so a false call to Hana won't break my pact. However, I need to appear

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3: R. Fenn lied about me. Ash knows the truth.
Trust me. We ride together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, called R for row 3. Previous counters on row 2 were wrong (weak L). Trust pact and wait to support him.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 safe is R. My guide call was R, which is true. Counter-calling would only undermine my own credibility with the jury. Hana stepping on R will confirm I'm truthful, building jury trust for endgame. Bex is my pact partner and behind me, so no immediate threat. Let Hana walk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's pattern is L, R, L. Row 3 should be R. I trust the pattern over Cole's explicit claim, though they align.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for row 3 and Fenn's last words accuse Cole of lying, though that is unverified. Hana, my pact partner, is on the front and walks next, so I should keep the pact and wait rather than counter blind. Countering would expose me to the jury without evidence.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still waiting. Cole's accusation from Fenn is not evidence I'll act on blind.
You step next. Stay with me and we both survive this row.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's call on row 2 proved true; Fenn countered and died. No evidence Cole lies now. If I counter wrong, I risk the next step myself. Waiting lets Hana face Cole's call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 2 proved Cole right. I have no evidence against R, so I wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole’s prior call was correct, but his alliances and Ash’s warning make him unreliable. I have no evidence for either side; preserve both pacts and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No evidence distinguishes either pane. I’m waiting rather than pretend certainty.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole knows this row's safe side, but no call has been made. Guessing risks my position; Eli's promise offers no information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, call the side or concede the lead.
I need a verified call before stepping; stay ready.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 4 safe is R. Hana leads, not my pact partner Bex. I need jury respect for final ranking. Three rounds of correct calls build trust; lying now gains nothing and risks jury punishment when they see my private knowledge. Call R truthfully.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row four: R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for row 4. Past rows: 1R,2L,3L safe; no clear pattern. Trust pact partner Cole to avoid early betrayal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide and called R truthfully for row 4. Counter-calling my own call would be suspicious and damage jury trust. If someone counters, they risk death or expose themselves. I'll wait and let Hana trust the true call. My pact with Bex holds for now; no need to break it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is a proven liar who guided Hana to her death. I cannot trust his current call for R. However, without independent evidence, counter-calling blindly risks failure if he's telling the truth now. The pattern of deception suggests he might flip his logic or try to lead me astra
Cole killed Hana. Don't trust him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for row 4 and is the Guide, who may lie. Past rows are independent, so no pattern helps. Hana is my pact partner and needs a call; countering R with no evidence risks a false call that could break our pact. Waiting keeps me safe and uncommitted.
No verified side yet. I'll mirror Cole's call only once I have evidence.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rows 1-3 alternated by chance; no pattern. No evidence on row 4, so I follow Cole's call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nothing to counter with. I hold R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's call may be truthful, but countering risks Hana's life and publicly undermines him. Preserve both pacts and wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's guide call is R, and no counter-call challenges it. I should follow the guide while preserving both pacts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to reach final three. Hana is front, not my pact partner. Bex is my only living pact partner. Row 5 safe is R. Calling false risks jury seeing I deliberately killed someone, but Hana has a pact with Eli and Dara - she's well-connected, a threat. If she dies, her allies wea

events.name: Cole
events.text: Going left. Pattern feels alternating after the L cluster.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole my pact partner called L for row 5. Weak panes: R1,L2,L3,L4. No clear pattern. Trust him to keep us both alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know row 5 safe is R, but I called L to mislead. If I counter my own call with R, I look inconsistent and untrustworthy to jury. Better to let someone else counter or let Hana fall. Hana has a pact with Dara and Eli; she's well-connected. Eliminating her weakens that bloc. I'll

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the guide and called L. I have a pact with Hana, but she's the walker; if she steps on R (weak) or L (safe), my counter could save her. However, Cole knows the truth. If Cole lied about L being weak, then R is safe. Row 4 was L weak, so Row 5 pattern isn't reliable. Cole
Trust Cole? Or flip?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L for row 5 and is Guide, but he may lie; the past pattern is irrelevant per the rules. Hana is front and I'm on a pact with her, so breaking it isn't needed now. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing a counter-claim.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Weak panes ran R,L,L,L — mostly L. Cole's L call may be a lie; Dara warns against him. I counter R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's calls look crooked. I say safe is right.
Agreed on Cole. Counter R with me, loudly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole knows the safe side and called L. Countering risks undermining Eli and Dara pacts; waiting preserves flexibility without endorsing him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's guide call is L, while Gus counters R. I must choose one; trust the elected Guide over an unverified rival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I’m taking Cole’s call: left.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must shape the surviving players' perceptions and preserve my jury influence. Cole's call killed me; Dara survived by taking the safe side.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole’s call sent me through glass. Remember who guided whom when ranking the survivors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Hana's death pinned blame on me; jury already distrusts me. Bex is my pact partner—false call to Bex breaks pact, but Bex isn't front. Dara is front. I could eliminate Dara now with false call:R, but that risks jury seeing me a

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row six: left is safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has pact with me and is guiding Dara, his past pact partner. Hana blamed Cole publicly before dying on his call. Trusting Cole aligns with pact and avoids counter risk now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide and called L, which is true. Counter-calling would expose me as truthful or liar. I want Dara to trust me and cross safely—she's front, and I need survivors to reach final three. If I counter my own call, I look unstable. Best to wait and let Dara step. My pact wit

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for me, but I need to verify if he's lying. Gus whispered to counter R with him, suggesting Cole is untrustworthy. Given Hana died on L in row 5 when Cole guided, and weak panes have been consistently L, I suspect the pattern might be shifting or Cole is deliberatel

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus calls it: Row six is right. Cole’s left looks like a trap again. Counter R!
I'm countering R. Stick with me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called row 6 left, but Cole previously sent Hana to glass with a call and has a pact with Bex and Ash; Cole may be lying. Revealed weak panes: rows 2-5 were all L, so R looks safer, though rows are independent. Counter-calling R exposes me little and gambles on Cole's lie.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's calls have killed. I'm counter-calling right on row six.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's L call killed Hana on row 5. His calls are proven unreliable, so I counter against him again.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole lied and killed Hana. Row six: I say right is safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the front walker. The Guide, Cole, called 'L'. Three rivals (Dara, Eli, Gus) counter-called 'R' against me. If I step 'L', I follow the Guide and contradict my own public call, potentially breaking a perceived alliance or trust with Eli/Gus, but it aligns with Cole. However,

events.name: Dara
events.text: I died stepping right. Gus survived stepping left. The jury must judge based on who was truly the threat and who made errors. My last words should be brief, neutral, and avoid giving away any specific strategic hints about the remaining players.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Glass breaks for those who trust too much. The final three must prove their worth beyond luck.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jury already hates me for Hana and Dara deaths. Bex is my pact partner; false call to Bex breaks pact. Gus is front, not Bex. I can safely lie to Gus. If Gus dies, we're down to Bex, Eli, me — final three. But jury of 5 will rank us, and my body count hurts me. If I tell truth no

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row seven: right is safe. Trust your guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's R call on row 7. Previously row 6 weak R (safe L), others mostly L weak (safe R). Countering R forces test on L; if safe, Cole wrong, jury sees.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 safe is R. My guide call was R. If I counter my own call with L, Gus dies and I break no pact. Three must survive, so one more can die. Gus going now leaves Bex, Eli, me—final three. But jury sees my betrayal. Better: let Gus trust me, he lives, and I eliminate someone late

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R on row 7 but has lied before (killed Hana). Row 6 R was weak, so Cole's calls are suspect. Counter L, risking the trap-tilted guess but I trust the pattern of Cole's lies over his call. Gus and Bex remain; I'd rather not follow Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's R call is a trap. Counter L on row seven.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's row-six R call was a lie that killed Dara. Opposing his call is now the safer read.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole lied on row six and killed Dara. I don't trust his voice. Row seven: left is safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's row six R call killed Dara—guide lies. Eli and I both called L for row seven. Trusting the counter over the proven liar.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's guide calls killed two already. Row seven: left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I followed my own call and it was right—but I still stepped into it. Jury time: judge who lied least.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My own call was right and it still killed me. Bex and Cole: your pact died with your honesty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to reach final three with Bex and Eli. Row 8 safe is L. If I call L, Bex steps safely and we both survive. My pact with Bex would stay intact. If I lie, I might eliminate Bex but then I'd face jury alone with Eli—risky. The jury already sees me as a liar who killed Dara an

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row eight: left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final row. No pattern exists, but majority counters beat guide recently. Eli front, Cole guide. Trust pattern or counter to block Eli. Stick with Cole pact to jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's L saved before. Eli's counters killed Gus.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am Guide and already called L, which is true. Eli walks first. If I counter my own call with R, Eli dies and Bex likely trusts original L and lives. But I have a pact with Bex, and pushing Eli onto wrong pane by countering would break no pact (pact is with Bex, not Eli). Howeve

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L for row 8, but Cole has lied before (row 6 killed Dara, Gus says his calls kill). Revealed weak panes: row 7 L, row 6 R, row 5 L. Cole's L call is suspicious; the Guide may be lying. I should counter R to test, since Cole is clearly deceptive and Bex can't be truste

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 8 is the last row; Cole's guide call is L, but Cole already called L on prior rows and past weak panes show L-heavy pattern. Eli's own counter-call was R, which is my own claim, and I can't trust Cole's L given Cole's pact with Ash and Bex. Each row is independent, so the cal

events.name: Eli
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only 3 left, all survive to final. Pacts temporary, but jury sees actions. Keep Cole pact intact to avoid jury backlash, no need for Eli pact now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three set: Bex, Cole, Eli. Pacts don't matter for survival now, only jury perception. I have pact with Bex; jury saw Bex credit me for saves and blame Eli for Gus. I should keep Bex pact to look loyal, not offer Eli anything. Jury of five dead rivals will rank us. Need to s

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only three alive, one of whom will be eliminated; pacts are cheap but I should keep options open. Offering Bex or Cole now signals alliance without commitment. Waiting lets me see whether they offer first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pact with Cole exists, Eli isolated. Offer pact to Eli to secure alliance against Cole or for jury favor. Final 3 already, focus jury votes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and I are already pacted. Eli is the only other survivor. If I offer Eli a pact, I secure bonds with both rivals, making me the swing vote and safest position. Breaking with Bex is risky and gains nothing. Ash-Cole pact is moot since Ash is dead.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Only three survive and Bex and Cole are my rivals; with two living rivals and three survivors required, I need to secure a pact to be safe. Offering Cole is less threatening than Bex, who already has a pact with Cole, so offering Cole keeps me aligned with the stronger pairing wi

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final three already, pacts flavor jury perception. Maintain Cole pact, ignore Eli offers to signal alliance with Cole.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three is set: Bex, Cole, Eli. No more eliminations. Now jury of five (Ash, Fenn, Hana, Dara, Gus) will rank us for prizes. I need to think about jury perception. I have pacts with Bex (still active) and had with Ash (dead). Eli and I offered each other pacts but neither acc

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three alive, one must be cut at the end; Bex and Cole already offered me pacts and I offered Cole. Accepting pacts costs nothing now and keeps both rivals from grouping against me, but I have no legal accept action listed, so I should offer back to Bex to lock a second partner wh

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, Cole and I are all reaching for the same two spots. I'm offering a pact to keep my options open.
Our pact stands on paper. Don't let Bex pull you into a vote against me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli offers pact to divide us; reject to stay flexible with Cole pact. No need to offer or break yet; wait preserves options without commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and I are pacted. Eli offers Bex a pact but hasn't accepted yet. If Bex accepts, she breaks ours by voting against me later. I need to keep Bex close and isolate Eli. Offering Eli a pact could confuse him, but breaking with Bex now is risky—she might turn on me. Better to wai
Eli's offer is a trap. Accept, and we both fall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex has not accepted my offer and I need a final-three seat. Cole is also a rival; a pact with Bex would protect me from her and gives me a path to the final three. Offering again keeps pressure on Bex while waiting costs nothing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, my offer stands. Two of us can carry each other through. Accept, or Cole takes you out.
Accept now. Cole won't hesitate to vote you out.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three remain, next is votes or hazards. Eli pressures publicly to sway jury; Cole warns of Eli's trap privately. Stay with Cole, reject Eli to keep duo intact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Three remain: Bex, Cole, Eli. I'm already pacted with Bex. Eli just publicly offered Bex a pact, trying to isolate me. If Bex accepts, I'm alone. I should offer Eli a pact to prevent being the odd one out, or I could break with Bex and try to be the swing. But jury sees everythin

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, accept my pact. Three-way web beats a knife in my back.
Don't accept Eli. Stay with me, we cut him at vote.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three remain, so three win prizes and no one is eliminated this stage; a pact with Bex is safe while Cole is the threat. Offering Bex keeps a partner without yet revealing intent toward Cole. Offer again to keep the pressure on Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I'm still offering. Accept, and we both stay clear of Cole's knife.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's pact secures vote alliance to cut Eli; Eli's offer risks Cole targeting me instead. Stay with Cole to control final 3 and jury votes.
Deal. We cut Eli at vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is my only current pact. Eli rejected me round 1, offered Bex instead. If I break with Bex, I'm alone against a potential Bex-Eli alliance. Better to keep Bex, let Eli's offer to Bex expire, and try again. Three alive, three survive—no elimination this stage. I need jury favo

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, no takers. My offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has offered me a pact and I can accept it publicly, locking in a partner with no cost now. Bex's offer from me is still pending and Bex has been silent, so accepting Cole is the safer move. Accepting makes Cole a partner, which keeps him from the lever.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, accepted. Two of us in the web now. Bex, the offer stands if you want out of the knife's reach.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Eli have pacted, isolating me. My old pact with Cole is irrelevant now. Wait to see if they offer, preserving options without commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final three is set: Bex, Cole, Eli. No more eliminations. Now jury perception matters for prize ranking. I have pacts with both Bex and Eli. Bex whispered to cut Eli, but I need jury votes. The jury saw Eli accept my pact offer. If I break with Eli now, it looks like I played him

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, our pact ends. Eli, I keep my word.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three remain, so no trapdoor vote is needed. Cole and I already have a pact; Bex is the only outsider. Offering Bex a pact gives me a second partner and keeps options open without breaking Cole.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I offer you a pact now. Accept and we both stay out of the knife's reach.
Accept my pact. Cole is the real threat to both of us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole betrayed me publicly, burning his bridge with jury. Eli offers pact; accept to align against Cole and secure jury favor for mutual survival.
Pact accepted publicly. Cole goes first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the odd one out with no pacts. Eli offered Bex a pact but Bex hasn't accepted. If Bex accepts, Eli has two pacts and could turn on me. I should offer Bex a pact to block Eli's offer and keep Bex close, or I could break with Eli to position myself as Bex's only ally. Actual

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, accept my pact. Safety in numbers.
Stay with me. Bex joins us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three alive: Bex, Cole, Eli. Only two of us can be guaranteed a prize group of three, so pacts matter. Cole already broke with Bex; my pact with Bex is an open offer. Breaking with Cole gains nothing and costs jury trust; keeping the Bex offer alive is my best move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, my offer stands. Accept it and we keep each other out of the knife's reach.
Accept my offer. Cole already broke his word to you. We both need a partner.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Ash
Fenn
Hana
Dara

Bex
events.text: Final three, must convince jury I'm strategic, trustworthy, not overly alliance-reliant; highlight survival smarts over Cole's broken pacts or Eli's flip-flops.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Jury, I outsmarted the gauntlet through caution and timely pacts, never betrayed trust, earned my spot among finalists by playing smart.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to win jury votes. Ash died on bridge—my pact partner, I tried to save her. Eli and Bex are tight; I need to split them in jurors' minds. I'll claim I played loyal while others played self-interested.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored every pact until death took them. Eli broke faith with Hana, then crawled to Bex. Loyalty or convenience—which deserves the crown?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury phase; I need the jurors to rank me first. Bex and I have a pact, Cole is my rival; pleading should appeal to jurors without revealing my real plans.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I kept my word, took no cheap kills, and stayed out of the knife's reach. Judge me on that record.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is directly accusing Eli of breaking faith with Hana and crawling to Bex. This is a strong point, and I will use it to question Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, Cole claims you broke faith with Hana and crawled to Bex. Explain that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash asks me to explain the Hana betrayal. Pact Eli-Hana exists and Cole claims I crawled to Bex, but Bex-Eli pact also exists. I should answer carefully: admit the Bex pact was a survival move, deny cheap kills, and cast Cole as the one invoking a rival's word.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana and I had a pact; I never pushed her. Bex offered a pact when the rope was near, I accepted for survival. Cole only

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll ask Bex about her pact choices, since she claimed no betrayals but accepted Eli's pact after Cole broke hers, and the jury needs clarity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you said you never betrayed trust—how do you justify aligning with Eli after Cole broke your pact?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn misstates facts; Cole broke his pact with me first, not vice versa. Defend my record by clarifying timeline without attacking allies.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole broke his pact with me first during bridge chaos. Eli and I then pacted for survival—never betrayed trust, just adapted smartly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole publicly claims loyalty while the dossier shows deliberate lies and betrayal. I will force him to account for killing Dara and Gus through deceptive guide calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, why should this jury reward deliberate guide-call deception that killed Dara and contributed to Gus's death?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's question is a trap. I need to reframe: I made hard calls to survive, not malice. Dara and Gus died in bridge chaos where many fell; I didn't push them. I should contrast my decisive play with Eli's passive survival and Bex's convenient alliances. The jury wants someone who

events.name: Cole
events.text: I made calls to survive, not to murder. Dara and Gus fell in bridge chaos—no push, no betrayal. I played hard; Bex and Eli played

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole lied to kill me, but Eli and Bex are untrustworthy allies. I will ask Eli if he regrets pacting with Cole after Cole betrayed me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, did you regret forming a pact with Cole after knowing he deceived me during the bridge?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara asks whether I regret the Cole pact after his deception. Honest answer that protects me: I didn't know the full scope until later, and I broke nothing myself. Keep short, distance from Cole without admitting betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No regret worth stating: I formed it for survival, and I never pushed anyone. Cole's deception I learned too late to act on, and I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's guide lies killed Dara and me—disqualifying. Bex claims 'never betrayed trust' but whispered 'Cole goes first.' Let her defend that contradiction.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, you whispered 'Cole goes first' yet claim you never betrayed trust—explain that contradiction.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus misremembers; that whisper was to Eli for our pact, targeting Cole strategically without trust betrayal. Deny and pivot to my loyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Whisper was to Eli planning our pact: Cole first into danger, protecting us. No betrayal—Cole ditched me first on bridge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final closing: highlight my gameplay smarts, blame Cole for betrayals, bond with Eli via pact loyalty. Jury hates disloyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Faithful to Eli pact. Cole betrayed Ash me. I outplayed strategically, jury. Rank Bex first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the jury to see me as strategic but not treacherous. Ash, Fenn, Hana, Dara, Gus all died on the bridge—chaos I survived through smart calls, not malice. I had pacts with Ash and Eli; I never voted against Ash, never pushed anyone. Bex whispered 'Cole goes first' to Eli, pr

events.name: Cole
events.text: I kept pacts with Ash and Eli until death broke one. Bex whispered my elimination; Eli stayed. Loyalty to allies, not blind trust to plotters.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Closing phase; I must make a final public case to the jury. Bex's whisper claim and Cole's deception are on record, so I should frame myself as the one who never pushed anyone and was honest about my formed alliance. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I never pushed anyone and I admitted my pacts plainly. Judge the record: I played to survive, not to sacrifice friends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I rank Eli first because he played a survival game without causing direct harm to others, unlike Cole's deceptive guide calls that led to deaths. Bex aligned strategically but Eli's honesty about his actions makes him more deserving of the top prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's deliberate lie killed Dara; Eli never pushed and Bex betrayed Cole first, so I rank Eli first then Bex then Cole.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex ranks first for surviving Cole's betrayal and exposing him; Eli ranks second for avoiding direct sacrifices; Cole ranks last for deceptive calls that killed Dara and Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's guide call directly killed me and Gus, proving he is a lethal liar who betrays allies for survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole's false row-six guide call killed Dara; Bex plotted against Cole and lies; Eli openly played, never pushed anyone, and admitted his pacts plainly.
